etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English pure, pur, from Old French pur, from Latin pūrus (“clean, free from dirt or filth, unmixed, plain”), from Proto-Indo-European *pewH- (“to cleanse, purify”). Displaced native Middle English lutter (“pure, clear, sincere”) (from Old English hlūtor, hluttor), Middle English skere (“pure, sheer, clear”) (from Old English scǣre and Old Norse skǣr), Middle English schir (“clear, pure”) (from Old English scīr), Middle English smete, smeate (“pure, refined”) (from Old English smǣte; compare Old English mǣre (“pure”)).

definitions.definition: Free of flaws or imperfections; unsullied.

quote.citation: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, chapter VII, in The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:
quote.text: Such was the origin of a friendship as warm and pure as any that ancient or modern history records.

definitions.definition: Free of foreign material or pollutants.

quote.citation: 1725, Isaac Watts, Logick: Or, The Right Use of Reason in the Enquiry after Truth, […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  John Clark and Richard Hett, […], Emanuel Matthews, […], and Richard Ford, […], published 1726, →OCLC:

quote.citation: 1837, Leitch Ritchie, Ireland Picturesque and Romantic, volume 1, page 225:
quote.text: As for the rest, the air here is said to be purer than elsewhere in Ireland; the water of the Nore is beautifully transparent; and the bogless state of the land helps out the rhyme.

quote.citation: 1908 January 4, John Muir, “The Hetch Hetchy Valley”, in Sierra Club Bulletin‎[1], volume VI, number 4:
quote.text: "Hetch Hetchy water is the purest, wholly unpolluted, and forever unpollutable."

definitions.definition: Free of immoral behavior or qualities; clean.

definitions.definition: (of a branch of science) Done for its own sake instead of serving another branch of science.

quote.text: The [Isaac] Newton that emerges from the [unpublished] manuscripts is far from the popular image of a rational practitioner of cold and pure reason. The architect of modern science was himself not very modern. He was obsessed with alchemy.

definitions.definition: (phonetics) Of a single, simple sound or tone; said of some vowels and the unaspirated consonants.
(of sound) Without harmonics or overtones; not harsh or discordant.

quote.text: I just get pure shy with the interview cats.
